The new Sovereign Network Interoperability platform aims to help institutions settle securities, exchange currencies, and move collateral across separate blockchain networks.

Its bridgeless design keeps assets on their original ledgers while coordinating transactions between approved counterparties. Consensys says the system uses cryptographic verification to reduce reliance on additional trusted intermediaries.

The platform targets four major financial workflows, including securities settlement, wholesale payments, collateral mobility, and tokenized fund transactions.

Consensys plans to support Ethereum-compatible networks and protocols such as the Ethereum Economic Zone and Inter-Blockchain Communication. Canton connectivity is also planned.

The launch builds on Consensys’ existing institutional infrastructure, including Linea, Hyperledger Besu and Teku. The company is positioning itself as a technology provider for financial institutions seeking private, always-on blockchain settlement.

#5318. Clock Ticking on Zcash’s Sprout Pool: 22,263 ZEC Unmoved Ahead of NU7 Lock

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Daily pool data shows Sprout holders moved more than 300 ZEC out in a September rush, then almost stopped. The last withdrawal was on October 19.

Unless someone acts in the next few days, nearly all of what remains will be unspendable at block 3,543,405.

Most coverage of Zcash's upcoming Sprout freeze quotes the same figure, about 22,000 ZEC. That number is accurate, but it is a single snapshot. It doesn't show whether the people who own those coins are doing anything about the deadline.

We checked the pool every day, and the answer so far is no.

According to ZecStats' daily value-pool records, Sprout has held exactly 22,263.34162335 ZEC since October 19. That is 11 straight days, and more than 12,000 blocks, without a single zatoshi leaving the pool. Our October 25 piece recorded the drop from 22,309 ZEC to 22,263 ZEC. Since then the balance hasn't moved.

ZecStats publishes a daily CSV of every Zcash value pool, using the last block of each UTC day. Its figures follow the valuePools field that a full node returns through the getblockchaininfo call. The archive starts on July 30, 2026, and gives a 92-day picture of the Sprout pool.

Across those 92 days, about 374 ZEC, or 1.65% of the pool, left Sprout. That is an average of roughly 4 ZEC a day. The average hides the real pattern, though: the pool moved on only 15 of the 92 days.

Most of the withdrawals came in a few large transfers in September:

Together with smaller moves on August 31, September 17 and September 19, the 30 days to September 29 saw 310.5 ZEC leave Sprout. That is about 10 ZEC a day.

October was much quieter. Apart from one withdrawal of 46.05 ZEC on October 19, the month's activity was small change:

Since October 19, there has been no movement at all.

At September's pace, about 70 ZEC more would leave before activation. At October's pace, it would be well under 15 ZEC. On the last 11 days' pace, the answer is zero.

The deadline is set in ZIP 259, which defines how the NU7 network upgrade is deployed. It sets the mainnet activation height at 3,543,405.

NU7 does not introduce a new transaction format. Instead, after activation, version 4 transactions become invalid, while versions 5 and 6 remain valid. Sprout's design is the problem. As ZIP 259 puts it: "Because Sprout transfers can only be represented by version 4 transactions, funds remaining in the Sprout pool become unspendable."

The coins would not be destroyed, and NU7 does not change Zcash's supply cap. They would simply be stuck in a pool that no valid transaction can spend from. Today the stranded amount would be 22,263 ZEC, about 0.13% of the roughly 17.01 million ZEC in circulation.

ZIP 259 also skips Zcash's usual three-month gap between the first supporting software release and activation. Operators running unsupported software could stay online and follow a pre-NU7 chain.

As of ZecStats' latest update on October 30 at 13:09 UTC, the chain was at block 3,535,877. That leaves 7,528 blocks until activation.

In October, the network averaged about 1,147 blocks a day, or one roughly every 75.3 seconds. At that rate, block 3,543,405 arrives around 02:00–03:00 UTC on November 6. That is the evening of November 5 in the Americas and the early hours of November 6 in Europe and Africa.

Small changes in block times could move that window by a few hours. Holders who plan to move funds on the final day risk missing the cutoff.

In practice, getting funds out of Sprout means sending a version 4 transaction that moves them into a newer pool before activation. Users need software that can still build Sprout transactions and a synced node or wallet that recognizes their old notes.

The September withdrawals show that some holders are still paying attention. Several were round amounts, such as 99.998 ZEC, which is consistent with someone moving 100 ZEC and paying a fee. The 11-day pause since October 19 suggests something else: most of the remaining 22,263 ZEC may belong to keys that are lost, forgotten or no longer used.

That has been part of the debate about Sprout for years. A pool that has been shrinking slowly since Zcash's early days is now on a fixed timetable. The daily data indicates that most of its remaining balance is not being moved.

Every report that cites "about 22,000 ZEC at risk" is technically correct. The more useful figure for anyone tracking the upgrade is the rate of change, and right now that rate is zero.

The useful thing to watch over the next week is whether the Sprout line in ZecStats' daily data moves again before block 3,543,405. If it doesn't, Zcash will activate NU7 with about 22,263 ZEC permanently locked in its first shielded pool. That would be one of the largest deliberate freezes of user funds by any major blockchain upgrade, and nearly all of it would be coins whose owners did not move them in time.

Tether’s growing Bitcoin holdings are backed by a highly profitable stablecoin business. The company generated $4.5 billion in net operating profit during the first nine months of 2026, including $1.5 billion in the third quarter.

USDT issuance remained near $184 billion during the period, while Treasury bills and reverse repurchase agreements continued generating most of Tether’s income.

Tether’s third-quarter attestation showed $191.45 billion in reserve assets against $183.50 billion in liabilities. Its excess reserves climbed to $7.95 billion, nearly doubling from $4.1 billion at the end of June.

The company also reported $132.4 billion in direct and indirect US Treasury bill exposure, giving it a substantial source of recurring income.

This business model separates Tether from companies that raise capital specifically to buy Bitcoin. Strategy has relied heavily on stock sales and debt offerings to expand its treasury, while Tether can allocate a portion of its operating profits toward BTC.

Tether latest disclosure also puts its Bitcoin holdings above the amount listed in its third-quarter USDT reserve report. That report valued Bitcoin reserves at $8.37 billion on September 30, while Ardoino’s estimate puts the company’s total position near $11.5 billion.

Tether’s growing Bitcoin treasury shows how stablecoin profits can fund a major corporate crypto position. With USDT remaining one of the industry’s largest dollar-backed tokens, the company has a recurring earnings engine supporting its long-term Bitcoin strategy.

Strategy still holds a much larger stack, but Tether has emerged as a powerful corporate Bitcoin holder in its own right.

#5316. Why Coinbase Bitcoin Discount Just Hit a Yearly High

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. Classic crypto market metrics have suddenly stopped reflecting reality. Bitcoin’s discount on the U.S. exchange Coinbase relative to the international Binance has hit a yearly high, with the Coinbase Premium Index collapsing to around −0.06%.

In normal times, such a chart gives traders a cold sweat: the index going deep into the red zone means that large funds in the U.S. have started massively dumping crypto.

However, the current collapse of the indicator turned out to be a technical illusion. It was provoked by the emergency freeze of operations on Binance immediately after a large-scale hack of the exchange, which completely blocked classic cross-exchange arbitrage.

The anomalous price gap coincided with the largest incident in the industry’s history: on October 29–30, hackers attacked Binance’s hot wallets, withdrawing about $6.3 billion. The exchange promptly froze half of the stolen funds on the blockchain, and the head of the platform promised to fully cover the remaining client losses from the SAFU reserve fund.

Nevertheless, amid the panic, the price of Bitcoin dropped to $77,000–$78,000.

To localize the problem, Binance completely shut the gateways — it temporarily banned any deposits and withdrawals of funds. This decision instantly paralyzed cross-exchange arbitrage. Large players physically could not buy the temporarily cheaper Bitcoin on Coinbase and transfer it to Binance to even out the price.

Liquidity was locked inside the platforms, which caused the discount to artificially swell to its widest level in a year.

As noted by Galaxy Research’s head of research Alex Thorn, due to the blocking of transactions, the discount on Coinbase temporarily stopped being a signal of weak demand in the U.S.

On November 1, Binance announced a phased reopening of withdrawals, starting with BTC and ETH. Now the market is waiting to see how quickly arbitrageurs eliminate the gap. If the gap closes in the coming days, it means the anomaly was purely technical.

If the negative spread becomes entrenched, it will be an alarming signal of a real cooling of American capital.

Frustration is growing among parts of the XRP community, with one investor accusing Ripple of prioritizing its dollar-pegged RLUSD stablecoin ambitions and leaving longtime XRP holders behind. In an emotional appeal, the investor called on the company’s leadership to recognize the community’s years of loyalty and take action to help unlock XRP’s long-anticipated $20 valuation. The message has reignited debate over whether Ripple’s expanding business strategy will ultimately translate into meaningful gains for XRP holders.

Specifically, he accused Ripple of redirecting XRP’s economic and technological potential toward the stablecoin and other enterprise initiatives, arguing that the company was securing its own future while leaving longtime investors behind.

Scudu said the community had stood by Ripple through nearly a decade of negative sentiment, financial uncertainty, and its prolonged legal wrangle. Scudu accused Ripple’s leadership of securing the company’s future while leaving longtime XRP holders uncertain about their own financial prospects. He urged the executives to acknowledge the community’s loyalty and sacrifices, arguing that investors deserve to benefit from the ecosystem they helped support through years of challenges.

Garlinghouse also described XRP and RLUSD as “very complementary,” arguing that the two assets serve different but interconnected purposes within Ripple’s broader payments strategy. While RLUSD offers the price stability needed for payments and financial transactions, XRP can provide liquidity and facilitate value transfers across the XRP Ledger.

Garlinghouse further reassured the XRP community that Ripple’s business decisions would not come at the expense of XRP. He stressed that the company “will never do something we think is bad for the XRP ecosystem,” reinforcing his position that RLUSD’s growth is not intended to undermine XRP.

Ultimately, the debate goes beyond Ripple’s growing business footprint. What matters to XRP holders like Scudu is whether that expansion will create meaningful demand for the token itself. More partnerships, payment channels, and RLUSD adoption may strengthen Ripple’s ecosystem, but none of these developments guarantees that XRP will capture enough value to reach the investor’s $20 ambition.

#5314. Nvidia, Nike and 48 Other Companies Oppose OKX Stock Tokenization Plan

A total of 50 companies, including Nvidia (NVDA) and Nike (NKE), have officially raised objections to the trading of tokenized shares on a new platform backed by crypto exchange OKX and the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).

As per the most recent public notice by the joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), OKXICE, the total number of companies objecting to the initiative has reached 50 as of Oct. 30.

The total increased from 38 companies on Oct. 28, with 12 additional companies raising objections in just two days.

The new names that recently raised objections include Nvidia, Nike, Costco (COST), Micron Technology (MU) and Reddit (RDDT).

Other companies that have recently raised objections include cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike (CRWD), Corning (GLW), Bloom Energy (BE), IREN (IREN), USA Rare Earth (USAR), Palo Alto Networks (PANW) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE).

Big names in the financial world, including JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Goldman Sachs (GS) and Wells Fargo (WFC), have also raised objections.

Some other prominent names include Walmart (WMT), Coca-Cola (KO), McDonald's (MCD), Eli Lilly (LLY), Adobe (ADBE) and Dell Technologies (DELL).

OKXICE is a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE). Each of them owns a 50% stake in the joint venture.

The goal is to enable tokenized versions of traditional US stocks to be traded on the blockchain.

Instead of buying these shares on a traditional brokerage platform, eligible investors can trade blockchain tokens that represent ownership interests in the underlying securities.

The platform will be open 24 hours a day, seven days a week, as per the company's public notice.

The planned platform will be based on a temporary regulatory exemption issued by the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Sept. 17.

However, the regulator gave companies the option to object to any unauthorized third-party tokenization of their shares.

If a company submits an objection within the specified timeframe, then its third-party tokenized shares cannot be offered by the platform under the exemption.

#5312. Crypto Stocks Edge Up Before the Bell as 50 Companies Now Block Tokenized Shares: What Is Happening in the Market?

Crypto stocks edged higher before Tuesday’s open, November 3, even as Nvidia, Costco and Nike joined the companies blocking tokenized versions of their shares on OKXICE, taking the count to 50, and an AI chip sell-off sent Seoul’s Kospi down 3.6%.

The bounce is small, and it follows a bad month. Coinbase traded at $138.74 at 13:00 UTC, up 0.7% from Monday’s close of $137.83, its lowest finish since February 2024. Robinhood, Strategy and Circle rose between 0.5% and 1.1%, and Galaxy led with 2.8% after losing 8.8% on Monday.

The bigger story for the sector is the pushback against tokenization. Objectors to OKXICE, the 24/7 venue for tokenized US stocks that OKX is building with NYSE owner ICE, went from 16 to 50 in 11 days. Today is the deadline for companies notified on October 4, so the list could still grow, while Coinbase, Robinhood and the other crypto names on it have yet to say no.

Asia offered no lift. After a 1.1% drop in the Nasdaq on Monday, Samsung and SK hynix dragged the Kospi to 5,648.79, Shanghai slipped 0.8%, and Tokyo was shut for a holiday. Only Hong Kong closed higher, and Bitcoin held steady through the session at $77,326.

Investors are DUMPING US tech stocks at a rapid pace:The Nasdaq 100 index has dropped -6.1% over the last 3 trading sessions, its biggest 3-day decline since the April 2025 Liberation Day selloff. $QQQ This also marks the 3rd-largest 3-day decline since the 2022 bear market.… pic.twitter.com/jNvmex3HZj

So why are so many companies saying no to tokenization, and why are markets red from Seoul to New York?

Because they would carry the risk and see little of the benefit. OKXICE, the venue OKX is building with NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange, wants to offer round-the-clock trading of US stocks as tokens, paid for in stablecoins.

Under the SEC’s exemption, a company can keep its shares off such a venue if an outside firm does the tokenizing. It has 30 days from notice to object, and the objections have come fast:

The newest 12 are Nvidia, Costco, Micron, CrowdStrike, Corning, IREN, USA Rare Earth, Bloom Energy, Nike, Palo Alto Networks, Reddit and Hewlett Packard Enterprise. They join Microsoft, Alphabet, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan, which runs its own blockchain unit and says it still likes the technology.

The fight is over shareholder rights, especially votes. “Right now companies like Goldman and Microsoft see all of the risk and none of the upside,” Injective’s COO Mirza Uddin told CNBC.

OKXICE co-chair Andrew Cuomo isn’t backing down. “We are at the very beginning of the rollout of fundamentally different market structure,” he said at the October 30 press conference.

Discover: JPMorgan and Coca-Cola Block Tokenized Stocks on OKXICE as Objectors Hit 33. Coinbase and Robinhood Stay Out of the List

Only the crypto names avoided objection to tokenisation, along with several major US stocks. Coinbase, Robinhood, Circle, Strategy, BitGo and Securitize remain outside the objection list, as do Apple, Amazon, Tesla, SpaceX and Netflix.

One crypto-born company did say no. IREN, the Bitcoin miner that now earns more from renting computers to AI firms than from mining, objected in the latest batch.

Silence isn’t a yes, though. Venues get up to five business days to publish objections, so companies that answered this week may not show up until next week’s notice, and staying off the list doesn’t guarantee a stock will trade at launch.

The AI trade is cracking again. Big Tech results last week showed Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft will keep spending heavily on data centres and chips, and investors want to see faster returns first.

Monday’s selling on Wall Street, where the Nasdaq fell 1.1%, hit Asia’s chipmakers on Tuesday:

Seoul’s slide is the one to watch. The Kospi closed at a record 9,114.55 on June 22 and is now 38% lower, with 17% of that lost since the end of September.

Oil added to the strain. Brent climbed 1.7% to $106.58 after reports of limited US strikes on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz, a day after it fell more than 7% on hopes of new talks.

Hong Kong’s crypto stocks split. Exchange operator OSL rose 0.4%, and Boyaa Interactive, which holds Bitcoin, fell 5.1%.

They have been sold off with tech, then sold again for crypto. Every big name is down at least 12% since the end of September, and the first trading day after the Binance hack was the worst of the run.

Coinbase’s daily chart shows how far the slide has gone. The stock is $34 under its 50-day average and more than $50 under its 200-day, and Monday’s close was the lowest since February 2024.

COIN 1D chart. Source: Yahoo Finance (Nasdaq).

Discover: Crypto Stocks Lost Up to 54% in October as Hedge Funds Erased Every AI Stock Purchase Since 2025: Why Did Bitcoin Miners Fall Hardest?

The tokenization fight won’t move share prices on its own. For crypto stocks, today’s pre-market bounce still has to survive Wall Street’s open and a long night of election results.

Bitcoin (BTC) might not need another halving, another wave of institutional adoption, or even another round of monetary easing to deliver one of its most explosive rallies yet. Anthropic’s Claude AI predicts that it might need something considerably bigger: a fundamental shift in how the world’s largest economies treat Bitcoin.

Imagine the United States announcing a landmark expansion of its strategic Bitcoin reserve, followed by several major sovereign wealth funds committing billions of dollars to BTC.

Add a deterioration in confidence in traditional government debt and a sudden rush towards alternative stores of value, and Bitcoin could find itself at the center of an extraordinary financial realignment.

The most explosive scenario would begin with Washington committing to actively accumulate Bitcoin rather than simply retaining its existing seized holdings. An official purchasing program, potentially paired with incentives for allied nations to build their own reserves, could fundamentally change Bitcoin’s investment narrative.

The potential domino effect would be enormous:

Government adoption: The US establishes a long-term Bitcoin accumulation strategy, encouraging other nations to follow.

Sovereign wealth funds: Major investment funds in the Middle East and Asia begin allocating even small percentages of their portfolios to BTC.

Institutional FOMO: Pension funds, insurance companies, and asset managers accelerate allocations to avoid being left behind.

Monetary easing: Deteriorating government debt markets force central banks towards looser monetary policy, potentially increasing demand for scarce assets.

Bitcoin’s fixed supply of 21 million coins makes this particularly interesting. With approximately 450 new BTC entering circulation daily, a sudden acceleration in institutional and sovereign demand could create a substantial supply-demand imbalance.

From a technical perspective, Bitcoin would first need to reclaim the $80,000-$85,000 region and establish it as support. A sustained breakout above $90,000 would provide a much stronger bullish signal, potentially attracting momentum traders and sidelined institutional capital.

Beyond that, the $100,000 psychological milestone would become the next major battleground. A convincing weekly breakout, accompanied by expanding trading volume, a bullish MACD crossover, and RSI momentum returning to stronger territory, could provide the foundations for another major price discovery phase.

If institutional inflows accelerated alongside these developments, Bitcoin could potentially target $150,000 before entering an even more aggressive speculative rally.

The final leg towards $250,000 would require an extraordinary combination of sovereign adoption, institutional FOMO, and favorable macroeconomic conditions. This is not a technical outcome we can currently assume; it would depend heavily on the hypothetical catalyst materializing.

#5309. Circle Begins CCTP V1 Wind-Down Amid Doc Mismatch

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Burn limits on Circle's legacy USDC bridge began falling on October 31, and the V1 contracts pause on December 1.

On the same migration page, a block of instructions written for AI coding assistants still says Noble, Sui and Aptos "still require V1." Circle's own release notes say two of those three chains moved to V2 weeks ago.

Circle's legacy cross-chain transfer protocol entered its final month today. From October 31, burn limits on CCTP V1 start falling toward zero, and on December 1 the V1 contracts pause. Any app still using them will stop moving USDC between chains.

Most coverage has focused on those two dates. But the guide developers are told to follow, Circle's V1-to-V2 migration page, contains a mistake in the section written for AI tools.

Embedded in the page is an "Agent Instructions" block, guidance meant for AI coding assistants that read the documentation for developers. It says: "Noble, Sui, and Aptos still require V1." For two of those three chains, Circle's other published records say the opposite.

The schedule is fixed. Circle announced in an August 27 blog post that "CCTP V1 (Legacy) deprecation begins October 31, 2026 and completes on December 1, 2026."

From today, V1 burn limits fall, and the migration guide says "message limits will tighten over time until no new burns can be initiated." On December 1 the V1 contracts pause, and any integration still pointing at them can no longer transfer USDC between chains.

Circle has been firm about this. "Migration from CCTP V1 (Legacy) to CCTP V2 is required, not just recommended," the company wrote, adding that V2 "uses separate contracts and APIs and is not backward compatible."

Funds already in transit are protected. The guide says "all pending redemptions will remain available" during the phase-out, and that Circle "will maintain minter allowances greater than the total of pending attestations."

The migration page has two audiences. Human readers see the main guide. AI coding assistants also parse a separate instruction block, which tells them how to answer developer questions.

In that block, the guidance is clear: "Noble, Sui, and Aptos still require V1."

The main text above it says something different. According to the human-facing guide, "CCTP V2 contracts are available on all CCTP V1 chains except for Noble and Sui," and "Sui will be supported by V2 before the deprecation begins." Aptos isn't listed as an exception there at all.

So one page gives two different answers about the same chains, and the out-of-date answer is the one written for AI tools.

Circle's 2026 CCTP release notes show how out of date the instruction is:

Circle's supported chains and domains page now lists both Sui and Aptos in its CCTP table, with Standard Transfer support. The page's V1-only section names one chain: Noble.

As of today, Aptos has had V2 for more than two months and Sui for more than three weeks. The instruction telling AI tools that both "still require V1" was overtaken by Circle's own updates before the shutdown began.

Noble is the one chain in that line where the instruction is still accurate, and it is leaving CCTP entirely.

In a September 10 announcement, Circle said "Noble will not receive CCTP V2" and set out its exit:

For Noble, V1 is the only route available, and it is being closed.

A wrong line in documentation would normally be a small issue, but the timing makes this one more serious.

Many developers now ask AI assistants to write or update integration code, and those assistants read documentation like this page. A developer asking how to bridge USDC to Sui or Aptos could be told, based on Circle's own instruction block, to use V1. That is the route whose burn limits started falling today and which pauses in a month.

The fix in the code is not small either. Moving to V2 means:

An integration built on V1 now would have to be rebuilt within weeks.

For teams working with Sui and Aptos, the published records point one way: build on V2, using the contract addresses for domains 8 and 9. Don't follow the V1 guidance from the agent-instruction block.

For Noble, the deadline is January 12, 2027. Before then, integrators need to remove Noble as a CCTP route, and holders need to move or redeem their USDC.

For everyone else, the burn-limit reductions have started. December 1 is the last day V1 integrations work, and any app still on V1 after that will stop moving USDC between chains.

#5307. 40 Million XRP Moved From Binance Hacker Wallet

Blockchain tracking service Whale Alert has reported that a wallet linked to the massive $6.3 billion Binance hack has just sent 40 million XRP (~$50.5 million) to a mystery address.

On Nov. 2, Whale Alert shared information about the huge XRP transfer, noting that the transaction initiator is an address tagged "Binance Hack 2026."

The huge transfer took place at 03:56 UTC, Whale Alert data shows. The transaction involved 40 million XRP (~$50.46 million).

Interestingly, just 50 seconds before that, Whale Alert reported another transfer of 40 million XRP.

Another 40 million XRP (~$50.44 million) was also sent from the wallet tagged as "Binance Hack 2026" to a mystery address.

In total, these two transfers involved 80 million XRP (~$100.9 million).

Both transfers originated from the same wallet but were sent to separate mystery addresses.

It is still unclear why these transfers were made. There is no sign that these funds have been sent to a crypto exchange or sold yet.

The transactions took place just days after Binance faced one of the biggest cryptocurrency hacks ever.

The massive XRP transfers came shortly after Binance started to restore cryptocurrency withdrawals following the unprecedented security breach the cryptocurrency exchange faced.

On Nov. 1, Binance annonced that the exchange would restore withdrawals in phases for 15 blockchain networks, including XRP Ledger, Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain and Solana.

It also mentioned that withdrawals would be gradually restored for other networks, such as Tron, Dogecoin, Zcash, Avalanche, Sui, Polygon and Arbitrum.

The first stage of withdrawal resumption was set to take place between 06:00 and 09:00 UTC on Nov. 1.

After Binance faced a security breach on Oct. 29, which led to the loss of around $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from its hot wallets, it temporarily paused withdrawals.

The exchange noted that withdrawals would be restored gradually after the security and infrastructure checks had been performed.

Binance also said that XRP balances were already fully backed, as were those of other major cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and BNB.

Binance claimed that, as of Nov. 1, around 95% of affected assets had been replenished. The remaining 5% consists primarily of less liquid cryptocurrencies.

#5305. Brazil’s Largest Crypto Exchange Hit by Cyberattack as Losses Top $45M

Brazil’s largest digital asset exchange, Mercado, suffered a cyberattack that drained more than $45 million, adding to a string of crypto attacks in 30 days. Blockchain reporters have warned that repeated hacks hurt sentiment, regardless of which platforms cover the losses.

Blockchain security firms confirmed the attack, sparking fresh debates on the state of digital assets amid advanced bad actors’ tools. Initial research placed losses at $40 million, before Arkham Intelligence analyst Emmett Gallic reported an additional $5 million.

According to him, losses are growing, and bad actors are targeting old deposit addresses to sell off memecoins and altcoins. This adds to the growing list of digital asset exchanges hacked within a short period.

The exchange confirmed the incident to quell fears, adding that the attack method remains unknown. In a statement released on X, they stated that no harm was done to customers and there was no data breach.

However, they temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while the investigation and tracking continued. They later released a list of addresses where funds were stolen to widen community efforts in tracking.

“We continue working to safely restore operations and will keep our customers informed through our official channels. To contribute to the monitoring and tracking of assets on blockchain networks, we are sharing the destination addresses identified in the transactions related to the incident.”

The platform placed the value of assets involved at $38 million, and $11 million was blocked with the help of crypto firms including Circle, Tether, Paxos, Chainalysis, BRL1, etc.

“Update on the incident: Mercado Bitcoin assures you that you will not suffer any loss of assets due to the security incident we identified today on our platform.”

Last week, Binance faced the largest crypto breach, involving $6 billion in assets, although a large chunk was traced. This trumps Bybit’s infamous saga where bad actors drained nearly $1.5 billion.

The FBI and other intelligence agencies flagged North Korean hackers for the incident, calling for wider cooperation to tackle the recurring attacks.

Crypto policy watchers have warned against the hacks, especially on top platforms, as they crash broader market confidence. Users also pointed to growing AI tools and reiterated fears of Q-Day.

#5304. Hackers Use Claude, Gemini and Kimi to Identify Valuable Crypto Targets

Cybercriminals are using popular artificial intelligence (AI) models like Anthropic's Claude, Google's Gemini and Moonshot AI's Kimi AI to evaluate the financial worth of potential victims, including those owning cryptocurrencies.

Cybersecurity researchers at Cisco Talos detailed in a new report how a new type of Windows malware dubbed VOLTA-AUTODOXER, or simply VOLTA, steals sensitive data and uses AI tools to identify potentially lucrative targets among compromised users.

Compared to traditional information-stealing malware, which mainly steals passwords and credentials, VOLTA can also analyze stolen data to build victim profiles and determine what assets hackers can potentially exploit for profit.

Notably, one of VOLTA's most dangerous features is its ability to extract sensitive crypto wallet information, including recovery seed phrases, which can potentially give attackers access to digital assets.

VOLTA also includes features that can crack cryptocurrency wallet vaults, posing a big risk for people who store their crypto wallet credentials on their computers.

But its features are not just limited to stealing crypto.

As explained by Cisco Talos security researcher Ryan Fetterman, VOLTA can also grab saved browser passwords, payment card info, authentication tokens, email credentials and active sessions on popular platforms like Telegram, Discord, Steam and Roblox.

It can also extract info from Outlook accounts and Slack workspaces, as well as other personal and professional information on the infected system.

The malware also takes things further by analyzing victims' email accounts to grab more personal data.

For example, it can scan Gmail accounts for purchase confirmations and receipts from services like Amazon, PayPal, Walmart, DoorDash and Uber Eats.

This way, attackers can get more details about a victim's identity, home address, job and spending habits.

The malware can send stolen data to AI models via the OpenRouter service, which provides access to several AI models.

It first tries to process the collected data using Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6.

If the model fails to process the request, VOLTA is hardcoded to try Moonshot AI's Kimi K2 and Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash.

As explained by Cisco Talos, VOLTA specifically looks for refusal responses before attempting to use a different AI model.

It feeds the collected data to the AI models and asks them to analyze it, providing a comprehensive evaluation of a victim's financial worth.

It can also help identify valuable assets and then rank them based on how lucrative they may be. It can also score a victim's cybersecurity.

Essentially, it allows hackers to use AI models to find potentially lucrative targets without the need to manually sift through stolen data.

Bitcoin briefly dropped more than $2,000 after early election results pointed toward a Democratic victory, falling from nearly $78,000 to the $75,000 level. Buyers subsequently stepped in, lifting BTC toward $77,700 this morning.

The selloff extended beyond crypto markets. Nasdaq 100 futures dropped as much as 2.3%, while S&P 500 futures fell 1.3% as investors reacted to the possibility of tighter oversight of technology companies and AI infrastructure projects.

BREAKING: The S&P 500 is now on track to open below 7,500 for the first time since July 31st as markets price-in a Democrat victory in both the House and Senate.Nasdaq 100 futures are now down more than -2% tonight. pic.twitter.com/mBbq77a2mG

The dollar also weakened, while the 10-year Treasury yield slipped six basis points to around 4.90%. The moves raised concerns that a Democratic-controlled Congress could limit Trump’s tax and spending agenda, while increasing regulatory scrutiny across several industries.

Bitcoin’s decline followed an already difficult period for digital assets. The king had slipped below $77,000 earlier in the week as technology stocks weakened and investors reduced exposure to riskier assets.

The election adds another source of uncertainty, although Bitcoin’s recovery from its overnight low shows people have not fully abandoned the market.

The biggest crypto-specific concern involves the Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act, which aims to establish clearer rules governing digital assets and divide oversight responsibilities between U.S. regulators.

The legislation failed to advance through a Senate procedural vote in September, falling short of the 60 votes required. Democrats opposed the measure over concerns about ethics provisions and Trump’s crypto-related business interests.

A Democratic-controlled Senate could make the bill’s path more difficult, particularly if lawmakers prioritize stronger safeguards and additional oversight of the crypto industry.

The election also gives Democrats greater power to investigate the administration and examine potential conflicts of interest involving Trump’s digital asset ventures. Congressional scrutiny could intensify even without new legislation.

However, the result does not automatically mean crypto regulation will become more restrictive. Democrats have supported regulatory frameworks for digital assets, but disagree with Republicans over enforcement, consumer protections and safeguards against political conflicts.

The immediate risk is that negotiations become slower and more complicated, leaving crypto firms without the regulatory clarity they have sought.

Bitcoin price direction will likely depend on whether the election-driven selloff spreads into a deeper market correction. A sustained recovery in Nasdaq could help Bitcoin regain momentum, particularly if investors begin treating the election result as a temporary source of uncertainty rather than a lasting threat to risk assets.

On the other hand, continued weakness in technology stocks could pressure BTC and altcoins further. Investors will also watch whether Democrats pursue aggressive investigations or push for substantial changes to crypto legislation.

The political shift could create a more difficult environment for Trump’s crypto agenda during the final two years of his presidency. Yet a divided government may also limit sweeping policy changes from either party.

For now, Bitcoin price remains caught between broader market weakness and uncertainty over U.S. crypto regulation. The election has changed the political landscape, but the next moves in Congress will determine whether the impact becomes a lasting obstacle for the industry.

#5300. XRP Final Move: Binance Empties Hacked Wallet of Last $101 Million

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

The compromised hot wallet of the Binance exchange has been completely emptied. Blockchain tracker Whale Alert recorded two identical transactions of 40 million XRP each (around $101 million in total), which went to a new address 50 seconds apart.

This is the platform's corporate address rK21t6nGLy4MNDqhvy3pGwcLFy25qgfzMx. After the October 29 attack, the wallet received an official red "Reported as hacked" label in network explorers.

As a result of this final transfer, the address's balance dropped to 23.7 XRP (around $30) — the exchange fully removed the remaining funds, moving them to new internal wallets.

This transfer effectively closes activity on the vulnerable address and is a planned technical consolidation of the remaining balances. The transfer of assets followed a large-scale cross-chain attack on Binance that began on October 29. Total damage across ten different blockchains is estimated at $6.3 billion, making the incident the largest crypto theft in history.

Hot wallets on the XRP Ledger took the first hit: within five minutes at the start of the attack, a total of 233.46 million XRP (around $296 million) was withdrawn from them.

The specifics of the XRPL network itself oblige the exchange to fully zero out hacked addresses. Unlike most stablecoins (such as USDT or USDC), where issuers can forcibly freeze funds, the XRP Ledger code has no protocol-level blocking function.

Neither Ripple nor independent XRP Ledger developers has no technical ability to stop transactions, so leaving any available balance on a hacked wallet is unsafe. Moving the remaining 80 million XRP to new wallets isolated by the platform eliminates the risk of repeated withdrawals.

For the XRP ecosystem, this incident became an absolute all-time negative record, surpassing the September hack of the Bitget exchange, in which 103 million XRP ($157 million) was lost, multiple times over.

At the same time, no panic has been recorded on the market. Binance has fully restored withdrawal operations for clients. The platform's management officially stated that all net user losses will be compensated 1:1 from corporate reserves and SAFU fund money.

The transfer of the last $101 million in XRP likely puts an end to operations with the hacked address, minimizing further technical risks for the platform.

New account creation on the XRP Ledger jumped 142.4%, according to XRPScan data. It points to renewed interest in the ecosystem, even though XRP is still struggling to get its bullish momentum back.

XRPScan counted 7,734 newly activated accounts on November 1, 2026, up 33% from the day before and far above the network's 30-day average of roughly 3,500 new accounts a day.

Wallet creation is clearly speeding up. What's behind it is still unclear.

There are a few plausible explanations. Interest in tokenized assets, stablecoins, and decentralized finance apps on the XRPL may be pushing people to set up new wallets. Exchange onboarding and automated wallet creation could also be adding to the count.

But more accounts doesn't necessarily mean more users. One person can open several accounts, and automated systems can open many more, so other on-chain indicators are needed to judge real adoption.

XRPScan's history also shows account creation has spiked before, with an all-time high of about 30,600 accounts. The latest jump is well short of that.

The network numbers are growing, but the price paints a different picture.

TradingView data from November 2 shows XRP trading near $1.25, after a long correction from its September and October highs. It is still below several major moving averages, so bearish pressure continues to dominate the technical picture.

Immediate support sits around $1.20–$1.25. If XRP tries to recover, the $1.30-$1.35 region could act as resistance.

Rising account creation alongside falling prices reflects blockchain adoption and market demand, which are not the same thing. Stronger confirmation of growing XRPL adoption would need sustained growth in active addresses, transaction volumes, and general use of the ecosystem.

For now, the 142.4% increase is an encouraging sign of network activity. Whether it turns into real demand for XRP is still an open question.

#5298. Binance Says Its $6.3 Billion Hack Began With a Fake Job Interview, but Traders Aren’t Convinced

All reviews, research, news and assessments of any kind on The Tokenist are compiled using a strict editorial review process by our editorial team. Neither our writers nor our editors receive direct compensation of any kind to publish information on tokenist.com. Our company, Tokenist Media LLC, is community supported and may receive a small commission when you purchase products or services through links on our website. Click here for a full list of our partners and an in-depth explanation on how we get paid.

Binance said on Tuesday, November 3, that the Binance hack started with a fake job interview, in which North Korean hackers gave one of its engineers a coding test laced with malware, but many traders still doubt that is the whole story.

The October 29 theft took $6.34 billion from Binance’s hot wallets, the largest crypto heist on record. Binance’s incident report describes a campaign that ran for months: a tampered download in June, the fake interview in September and an internal AI tool that led the attackers to the engineers who ran its wallets.

Not everyone is buying it. Since the hack, traders on X have called it an inside job. They point to how fast the money left, across ten blockchains in about 20 minutes, and to how often Binance’s account has changed.

BREAKING: Binance says hackers used a fake job interview to infect an employee's computer.The malware let them hijack Binance's internal AI tool, take over more engineers' accounts, and drain $6.34 billion from its hot wallets.

No one has offered proof. The FBI has tied the theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, and blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs agrees with high confidence.

BNB hasn’t recovered either. It trades at $703.33, up 0.7% today but still 7.4% below its $759.85 close the day before the hack.

So what exactly does Binance say happened, and why are traders still unconvinced?

Slowly, through three engineers. Binance co-CEO Richard Teng told CNBC the attackers “spent months building their way in” and rejected the idea that a single laptop was the weak point.

“This wasn’t one mistake or one breach – it was a months-long campaign,” Teng wrote on X.

Binance says users won’t lose anything. It has replaced 98% of the stolen assets with its own funds, and about $2.85 billion has been frozen or intercepted with the help of Tether, Circle and others.

Discover: Bitcoin Settles Its $10.9 Billion Options Expiry Right on Max Pain After the Binance Hack

Because the doubts started before the report, and the report didn’t settle them. Two days after the theft, trader Financelancelot called it “totally an inside job,” and Solana trader Ansem wrote: “My trust in binance is gone.”

The skeptics keep coming back to five points:

The proof of reserves didn’t help. Binance’s November 2 proof used an October 31 snapshot, taken after it had already bought back most of the stolen coins, so critics say it can’t show how big the hole was.

A hack of this scale means serious security failures occurred. No platform is unhackable, but that cannot be an excuse. Every incident exposes weaknesses that should have been prevented.Some details are embarrassing. Public explanations also simplify what appears to have been a… https://t.co/ZMAjZt2hF8

Some of the louder claims have already fallen apart. A viral post blaming a North Korean “honey trap” passed 800,000 views before co-founder Yi He called it untrue and said ZachXBT, the investigator it quoted, never said it.

An employee’s laptop being the way in doesn’t make it an inside job. Fake job offers with booby-trapped coding tests are TraderTraitor’s best-known trick, the same group behind the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025.

Less than half of it has been stopped. Of the $6.34 billion taken, Binance says $2.85 billion has been frozen or intercepted, much of it stablecoins that Tether and Circle could lock.

The rest is on the move. Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic counts about $3.24 billion still in addresses linked to the attackers, and Chainalysis has found the stolen funds mixed with money from September’s Bitget exploit.

One pile hasn’t moved at all. The 233.46 million XRP taken from Binance, worth about $299 million, has sat in six wallets since November 2, untouched as of Wednesday morning.

Discover: Bitcoin Sellers Take a Week of Losses Below $80,000 as Strategy and Strive Keep Buying: Will $75,000 Hold?

More proof, and soon. Three things are due in the next few days:

Not yet. BNB fell 8.1% on October 29, from $759.85 to $698.46, on $414 million in volume, more than four times what it traded the day before.

It has leaned on its 200-day EMA ever since. BNB dipped to $680.74 earlier today, close to the $680 hack low, and bounced back to $703.33.

Binance has told its version of the Binance hack in detail. Until the independent review backs it up, traders will keep reading BNB’s chart as a vote of confidence.

#5295. Big Week Ahead as XRP Ledger Eyes Cleanup Upgrade

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

The XRP Ledger (XRPL) is set for a significant week ahead as its long-awaited cleanup upgrade heads for mainnet activation this week, bringing a wide-ranging collection of fixes and improvements to the blockchain.

The fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment, a collection of fixes for Single Asset Vaults, the Lending Protocol, Automated Market Makers, the permissioned DEX, trust lines, NFTs, MPTs, Escrow, Sponsorship, transaction signing, and permission delegation, is at the center of attention, with validator support putting it on track for a potential November 4 activation, provided the required voting threshold of 80% is sustained.

The earliest activation date is Nov 4, 2026 at 2:46 PM UTC, with just 2 days left according to the xrpscan countdown timer.

Some tokens on the XRP Ledger are supposed to be stored in accounts approved by their issuer; however, developers have found a few ways around that rule.

Issuers of regulated assets, such as stablecoins or tokenized funds, can require approval before anyone holds their tokens, typically to perform identity checks first.

Four proposed code changes would resolve the remaining exceptions. All four are included in a single network upgrade dubbed fixCleanup3_5_0.

These have not been merged into the XRP Ledger's main software yet. Once they are, fixCleanup3_5_0 requires support from more than 80% of the network's trusted validators for two weeks before being activated.

According to Hussein Zangana (Vet), director of community at XRP Ledger Foundation, there is a critical Linux kernel vulnerability on kernels 4.4+, affecting any unpatched Linux server in the world with an open IPv4 TCP port. For XRP Ledger node and validator operators who run RHEL 8/9/10, Debian 12/13, Amazon Linux, and Oracle UEK, a fix has already been shipped; they are simply expected to update and reboot.

For those who run Ubuntu, AlmaLinux, Rocky, CentOS Stream, this might not suffice, as they may need to take further steps until a fix is shipped for their distro. They should re-apply the nft rule after a reboot or a flush ruleset reload.

#5294. Akash’s Solana Migration Clears November 2 Vote at 97%, With Four More On-Chain Decisions Ahead

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

AKT stakers are close to approving Akash's move from Cosmos to Solana, with Mintscan projecting a pass at 97.2% yes as voting enters its final hours.

But a yes on Proposal 346 opens a door rather than completing a move. Before a single AKT reaches Solana, two independent audits and at least two more on-chain votes still have to happen.

The summary going around is simple: Akash is leaving Cosmos for Solana. The proposal itself is narrower than that, and the details matter for anyone holding AKT.

Proposal 346 on akashnet-2, titled "Migrate the Akash Protocol to Solana," closes at 15:02 UTC on November 2. A yes vote approves the migration plan and authorises AKT to launch as an SPL token through a one-way portal that stays open for two years. It does not set a cutover date, it does not move a single lease, and on its own it does not open the portal.

The technical spec for that portal was published the day after voting opened. It shows how many further steps lie between this vote and a working SPL AKT.

The proposal text in Akash's AEP repository says a yes vote does two things:

It also says plainly what it doesn't do: "it does not set a cutover date and does not move the marketplace." Live leases, staking and governance on akashnet-2 continue as normal. The marketplace moves only after audits and rehearsals pass and "a separate cutover proposal passes on this chain."

A no vote would stop the whole plan. In the proposal's words: "Nothing moves; the token does not launch and the program returns to option analysis."

At 08:43 UTC on November 2, about six hours before voting closed, Mintscan's page for Proposal 346 showed an expected result of "Will PASS":

Turnout stood at 68.80% of bonded stake, against a quorum of 33.40%. The same figures can be read from Akash's own chain API, through the proposal object and its tally endpoint.

Mintscan's 97.2% is yes as a share of all votes cast. Akash's pass threshold leaves abstentions out, and on that basis yes stands at about 98.7%, far above the 50% needed. The veto share is negligible.

The tally has barely changed since early morning. A read of the chain at 07:29 UTC showed almost exactly the same totals, with only a handful of AKT added to the yes side. With turnout and margin that large, the outcome is not in doubt. The more useful question is what happens after it passes.

The portal's design is in AEP-95, "One-Way AKT Sink to Solana,", a draft published on October 27 by core developers Artur Troian and Joseph Chalabi. It describes a "deliberately one-way" bridge with no return path. The authors say this removes "the largest class of bridge attacks."

Why supply doesn't change: every SPL AKT is backed by AKT locked on Akash, and nothing is minted independently on Solana. The token is a legacy SPL mint with six decimals and no freeze authority.

The spec's own risk table names the biggest trust point. The upgrade authority over the Solana programs could "mint without limit." That power is meant to sit with a time-locked multisig appointed by Akash governance, with monitors set to alert on every admin action.

At launch, SPL AKT has no protocol role. It will support "transfers and DEX liquidity only, with no staking or governance rights." Inflation stays on Akash. To seed trading, Overclock Labs, Akash's core developer, will send 1 million AKT through the bridge to a Solana treasury vault. That deposit follows the same rules as everyone else's.

Proposal 346 requires "two independent audits of the token and portal code before launch," with reports published within 30 days. AEP-95's launch sequence shows what that requirement means on-chain.

So Proposal 346 is the first of at least five on-chain decisions. The "2 to 3 weeks" launch estimate depends on the audits finishing and the upgrade and parameter votes passing on schedule.

For now, nothing. The proposal's disclosures set out what changes later:

Discussion of the proposal continues in GitHub Discussion #1123.

The proposal lists four items as "still open, to be settled and published before the cutover proposal":

The second item matters most to holders. The portal closes two years after launch, and the proposal doesn't yet say what happens to AKT that hasn't crossed by then. The final tally will confirm whether the plan goes ahead, but that answer, and the decisions in the votes that follow, will matter more to most holders than today's margin.

The proposal, known as HSP-029, passed with overwhelming support from NEAR’s House of Stake. It would gradually reduce the number of new tokens entering circulation, potentially strengthening the supply outlook as the network expands.

NEAR Plans to Take Millions of Tokens Out of Future IssuanceNEAR Protocol's (@NEARProtocol) $NEAR House of Stake has approved a proposal to reduce maximum annual token issuance from 2.5% to 1.6%.The change will roll out gradually over 24 months, reducing the issuance ceiling… pic.twitter.com/pmPOUrWhoI

The approved proposal would reduce NEAR’s maximum annual issuance rate from 2.5% to 1.6%, with the change phased in over 24 months. According to the proposal, the reduction could prevent 11.8 million NEAR from entering circulation during the first two years. Over six years, the avoided issuance could reach 66.1 million tokens.

At full implementation, daily issuance would fall from roughly 89,500 NEAR to 57,300 NEAR. The network would retain its existing distribution of newly issued tokens, with 90% going to staking participants and 10% allocated to the protocol treasury.

Beyond tokenomics, NEAR Protocol continues developing its chain-signature technology, which allows accounts to interact with external blockchains. NEAR Intents also supports cross-chain swaps, giving the ecosystem another potential source of activity and fee revenue.

The combination of lower issuance and expanding utility is giving NEAR crypto bulls a fresh narrative. However, the market will need to see sustained demand before the supply reduction translates into a lasting price trend.

The tokenomics overhaul gives bulls a fundamental catalyst, but traders will also need to see stronger spot demand and improving market momentum.

On the downside, a failure to hold the $3.70–$3.80 area could expose NEAR to another test of support near $3.50. Continued weakness across the broader crypto market would make a sustained recovery more difficult.

For now, NEAR Protocol has a clear catalyst in its issuance reduction proposal, alongside continued development of its cross-chain ecosystem. The next stage of the crypto rally depends on whether buyers can turn the tokenomics story into sustained demand and push NEAR beyond its immediate resistance levels.

#5291. Hong Kong Passes Its Crypto Tax Reporting Law: Exchanges Must Collect User Data From 2027 and Share It Abroad From 2028

All reviews, research, news and assessments of any kind on The Tokenist are compiled using a strict editorial review process by our editorial team. Neither our writers nor our editors receive direct compensation of any kind to publish information on tokenist.com. Our company, Tokenist Media LLC, is community supported and may receive a small commission when you purchase products or services through links on our website. Click here for a full list of our partners and an in-depth explanation on how we get paid.

Hong Kong lawmakers passed a crypto tax reporting law on Wednesday, November 4, requiring crypto platforms tied to the city to collect their users’ tax details from 2027, so tax officials can share them with other countries from 2028.

The law brings in the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, or CARF, the global standard for tracing crypto gains across borders. The government said Hong Kong’s Inland Revenue Department will start exchanging the data with partner jurisdictions in 2028.

The same bill updates the Common Reporting Standard, the system banks already use to report foreign accounts. Its new version, which also covers digital financial products, takes effect in 2028.

Hong Kong isn’t moving alone. It is one of 27 jurisdictions, including Singapore, the UAE and Switzerland, that have committed to first exchanges by 2028, the OECD’s latest list shows. Another 46, including the UK, the EU and Japan, start a year earlier.

So what does the new law ask of crypto platforms, and what changes for traders who use them?

It turns crypto platforms into tax reporters. The Inland Revenue Department’s CARF guide calls them reporting crypto-asset service providers: any business that carries out crypto trades for customers, whether as an exchange, a broker, a dealer or a crypto ATM operator.

A platform falls under Hong Kong’s rules if it is tax resident in the city, incorporated there, managed from there, or runs a branch or regular place of business there. Every platform that meets one of those tests has to register with the department, even if it has nothing to report.

Existing customers aren’t exempt. Platforms get 12 months after the rules take effect to collect self-certifications from users who already have accounts.

The law also sets offences for failing to register, skipping due diligence or filing wrong returns. Users can be prosecuted too, for knowingly or recklessly giving false information in a self-certification.

“Hong Kong has been supporting international efforts in enhancing tax transparency and combatting cross-border tax evasion,” said Christopher Hui, Hong Kong’s Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury.

Discover: Franklin Templeton Readies Two ETFs That Turn Stock Dividends Into Bitcoin as Washington Writes Crypto Rules Without Congress

On January 1, 2027, less than two months away. The bill moved quickly: a public consultation ran from December 2025 to February 2026, and the government published the bill on May 22.

Platforms that first fall under the rules in 2027 have until January 31, 2028, to register. The department hasn’t yet published the details of its online portal or the data format it wants.

Hong Kong is in the second wave. The OECD’s commitments list, last updated on September 14, splits the world like this:

Hong Kong’s rivals for crypto business are on the same schedule. Singapore and the UAE have also committed to their first exchanges by 2028.

Existing users will get the same request within a year. Lying on it is an offence under the new law, so ticking the wrong country isn’t a way around it.

That is usually enough for a tax office to spot crypto gains that never showed up on a return. Transfers to outside wallets are covered too, so moving coins off the exchange still leaves a record.

Platforms carry the heavier load. They have under two months to build the forms, the checks and the records, and the department has yet to publish its portal details.

For traders, Hong Kong’s crypto tax law closes one of the last big Asian gaps in the OECD’s reporting net. By 2028, a crypto account in Hong Kong, Singapore or Dubai will be about as visible to a home tax office as a bank account.

Lower exchange reserves generally mean fewer tokens are on hand to be sold. When investors pull SHIB into private wallets, there is less supply available to sellers on centralized exchanges. That doesn't guarantee a price recovery, but it can make the supply picture more favorable.

Immediate resistance sits around $0.00000500–$0.00000530. The $0.00000440–$0.00000450 region is the next potential support zone.

If demand starts to recover, the drop in exchange-held supply could matter more. For now, the 85 trillion mark is a constructive on-chain sign, not a confirmed bullish reversal. A more convincing case would need continued exchange withdrawals, stronger buying, and a move back above the key resistance levels.

Block DOJ settlement talks have reached a major turning point, with Jack Dorsey-owned payments company agreeing in principle to pay $764 million. The proposed deal would resolve a federal investigation into alleged failures in its anti-money laundering controls.

The agreement follows years of scrutiny over Block’s Cash App compliance practices. The company disclosed the development in its quarterly filing yesterday, outlining a deferred prosecution agreement with the U.S. Department of Justice.

Jack Dorsey’s Block has beaten Q3 earnings estimates, posting $3.2B in gross profit.The company has also raised its 2026 outlook, while warning that a potential DOJ settlement could be larger than expected.Strong results and a higher forecast from one of the biggest names in… pic.twitter.com/Bk0KByUDPV

The announcement arrives alongside a sharp decline in Block’s Bitcoin business. Bitcoin ecosystem gross profit plunged 50% year-over-year to $52 million during the third quarter, despite stronger overall company earnings.

The proposed Block DOJ agreement would defer prosecution for three years over allegations that the company failed to maintain an effective anti-money laundering program. The DOJ’s investigation centers on compliance requirements under the Bank Secrecy Act. Block would need to meet obligations outlined in the agreement throughout its term.

If the company fully complies, prosecutors would move to dismiss the deferred charges. However, the resolution remains subject to final agreement terms and court approval.

The proposed settlement carries a gross monetary component of approximately $964 million. Credits for previous regulatory resolutions would reduce the expected net payment to roughly $764 million. Block has already accrued $764 million for the matter as of September 30. The company warned that the final cost could exceed that amount.

The investigation dates back to 2023, when federal authorities began examining Block’s compliance practices and related disclosures. The scrutiny followed allegations raised by short seller Hindenburg Research.

Block rejected those allegations as inaccurate and misleading. Separately, New York’s financial regulator fined the company $40 million in 2025 over compliance failures.

The Block DOJ development comes as the company’s Bitcoin business faces a sharp profitability decline. Block reported Bitcoin ecosystem gross profit of $52 million in Q3, down from $104 million a year earlier. The company attributed the decline primarily to lower fees on certain Bitcoin transactions through Cash App.

Bitcoin-related revenue reached approximately $1.8 billion during the quarter. However, the lower fees significantly reduced the amount Block retained from its Bitcoin operations.

The weakness contrasts with stronger performance across the broader business. Block reported $3.24 billion in total gross profit, up 22% year-over-year. Cash App gross profit climbed 27% to $2.07 billion. Square gross profit increased 14%, while quarterly net income rose to approximately $566 million.

Block also raised its full-year 2026 gross profit forecast to $12.63 billion, representing expected growth of roughly 22%.

Now, proposed Block DOJ settlement creates a major legal expense alongside a mixed earnings picture. Its Bitcoin business is generating less profit, even as Cash App and Square support stronger company-wide growth.

#5287. XRP Targets Stripe’s $1.9 Trillion Payments Ecosystem as Ripple Integrates Privy Wallets

Ripple is expanding the XRP Ledger’s (XRPL) reach into digital payments through a partnership with Privy, the embedded wallet provider owned by Stripe.

Announced Tuesday, the integration will let developers build applications that support XRP, Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin, and other digital assets without requiring users to manage cryptocurrency wallets independently.

Notably, the partnership could make it easier for fintech companies to incorporate blockchain-based payments into their products, potentially giving XRP greater exposure to Stripe’s payments ecosystem. Stripe reported $1.9 trillion in payment volume during 2025, a 34% increase from the previous year, according to its annual update.

However, it’s important to note that, while the integration does not mean Stripe will process payments in XRP, it could broaden the asset’s reach by making XRPL-based applications easier to develop.  Under the agreement, developers can create wallets, sign transactions, and build services using XRP, RLUSD, and other supported assets.

Privy provides ready-made wallet tools that businesses can integrate into their apps, while allowing users to export their private keys and recovery phrases.

“Privy brings proven wallet infrastructure that makes it easier for fintechs and developers to bring XRPL into real products, from payments and stablecoin experiences to emerging forms of agentic commerce.” Markus Infanger, senior vice president of RippleX at Ripple said.

The companies also plan to introduce policy controls and gas sponsorship, giving developers more control over transactions while simplifying the payment process for users.

These features could support agentic commerce, where artificial intelligence agents make payments to purchase digital services or complete tasks. Privy’s server-side wallets would allow these agents to hold and transfer funds, while support for internet native payments (x402 payments) could enable automated transactions between online services.

For businesses that prefer to avoid cryptocurrency price volatility, the integration also supports RLUSD, Ripple’s dollar-pegged stablecoin. This could allow developers to build payment applications using a stable-value digital asset rather than relying solely on XRP.

Ripple’s move comes as competing blockchain networks pursue partnerships with established financial providers.  Just last month, the Cardano Foundation joined Mastercard’s Crypto Partner Program to explore blockchain applications across payments and financial services.

Cardano has also pursued stablecoin liquidity through USDCx and institutional asset support through Fireblocks, while its participation in the x402 ecosystem targets automated payments involving AI agents.

Ripple, meanwhile, has expanded its payment partnerships through a March 2025 collaboration with Chipper Cash to support crypto-enabled cross-border payments into Africa. In November 2025, Ripple, Mastercard, WebBank, and Gemini announced a collaboration to explore RLUSD settlement for Gemini credit card transactions.

Despite this, the crypto market stays in limbo, with most digital assets trading in the red at press time, including Cardano, which is down 1.29% in the last 24 hours to $0.19. Binance has published its latest Proof of Reserves report as of October 31, 2026. Judging by it, client funds are still fully backed — despite the largest hack in crypto history at the end of the month. Coverage for XRP is 100.99%, and for the Ripple USD (RLUSD) stablecoin, 100.83%.

A comparison of balances as of October 1 and October 31 shows how the exchange's liabilities and reserves changed after the October 29 attack: hackers then withdrew about $6.3 billion from its wallets across ten blockchains.

Immediately after the attack, Binance suspended withdrawals and deposits, so the growth of balances in Ripple assets occurred before the hack. October results:

The main thing in the report is something else: Binance confirmed full coverage of the ten most traded assets, including BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB and SOL — and did so just two days after the hack.

About $3 billion of the stolen funds was quickly frozen directly on the blockchains with the help of partners, including Tether, Circle and Ripple. To cover the losses and return reserves to 1:1, Binance allocated more than $6.34 billion of its own capital. This reserve included the SAFU fund, the Binance Futures insurance fund and retained earnings.

The remaining 5% of losses are in low-liquidity tokens: they are being quietly bought back through over-the-counter (OTC) desks so as not to crash spot prices.

Each client can verify their own balance: the report is built on Merkle trees and zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs). For the market, this case sets a new bar: an exchange is no longer judged by whether it gets hacked, but by how quickly it stops an attack and whether it has enough of its own money to plug the hole.

#5283. Binance’s $6.3B Hack Fix Is Coming Tomorrow: Why the ZK Math Doesn't Tell the Whole Story

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

On-chain data shows the attacker behind the $6.3 billion Binance theft depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses.

At the same time, Binance's first post-hack reserve snapshot shows its biggest assets covered with buffers as small as 2.7 ETH and $6 of USDT. Binance's full zero-knowledge proof of those figures is due by Tuesday.

Some of the money stolen from Binance has started going back to Binance.

Blockchain intelligence firm Arkham has flagged the entity it tracks as "Binance Hacker" depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses. Arkham says those addresses "likely represent nested service(s)." These are third-party exchanges that use Binance for liquidity and custody, giving their own customers deposit addresses that sit on Binance's infrastructure.

If Arkham is right, the hacker isn't depositing into an ordinary Binance account. The money would be going to smaller platforms that operate through Binance. Exchanges have long known this is a weak point for stolen funds moving into normal trading. Either way, Binance is now receiving stolen funds at its own deposit addresses while it works to show customers it has replaced what was taken.

The FBI has attributed the October 29 theft to North Korea. The deposits come at a sensitive moment. Binance has just published its first reserve snapshot since the hack and has promised a full cryptographic proof of it by Tuesday.

$4 million is a small slice of a theft worth about $6.3 billion, but it matters for two reasons.

It shows how the laundering works. Nested services are a common way into the regulated financial system. A third-party platform that relies on Binance for custody may run weaker identity checks on its own users. Funds deposited there can be swapped and withdrawn without the hacker ever opening a Binance account.

Binance can act on it. Binance can't freeze bitcoin and ether sitting in wallets nobody controls, and it doesn't control the stablecoins that issuers like Tether and Circle have frozen. Deposits that land at its own addresses are different: they are on Binance's platform, so Binance can freeze them itself. One of the first tests of how Binance handles the money still in the hacker's hands is whether it freezes these funds and identifies the services that own the addresses.

While the hacker's funds move, Binance has been rebuilding its reserves. Its proof-of-reserves page now shows:

The first page covers Binance's six largest assets. Customer balances are what users hold. Reserves are on-chain wallet balances, including assets held with outside custodians.

The second page has four more assets, and two of them stand out:

Why USD1 and RLUSD matter: these are two of the stablecoins whose issuers froze stolen funds after the attack. World Liberty Financial froze $27 million of USD1, and Ripple began freezing RLUSD the same night. Both now show reserves above what Binance owes customers.

Assets with outside custodians: part of several reserves sits with outside custodians rather than in Binance's own exchange wallets:

The striking part isn't that the ratios reach 100%. It's how closely they stop there.

Compared with October's report: Binance's previous monthly report, published in early October before the hack, showed BTC at 100.35% and USDT at 103.88%. ETH was already at exactly 100.00%. After the theft:

Not every asset is that tight. USDC, ZEC and BNB carry buffers of 1.3% to 6%. The thinnest buffers are in BTC, ETH, USDT and SOL, which are among the assets the attacker took in the largest amounts.

How Binance says it got here: the pattern fits Binance's account of replacing the stolen assets in stages. It reported 80% replaced on Friday, 90% on Saturday and 95% on Sunday. The remaining 5% is in less-liquid tokens it is still buying. The money came from:

Binance confirmed taking 7,499 BTC from SAFU and has pledged to refill the fund to about $1 billion.

What the snapshot can't show: it was taken a little over a day after the theft, once the rebuild was under way. It shows the balance sheet after the replacement, not how large the gap was on October 29.

Binance says the full proof takes 40 to 50 hours to compute. Its latest update says it will be ready "by Tuesday, 2026-11-03 (UTC)." The system is open source, in Binance's zkmerkle-proof-of-solvency repository.

What the proof guarantees, according to the project's circuit design document:

The design also guards against a "dummy user attack" identified by Ethereum Foundation researcher Enrico Bottazzi. In that attack, fake accounts holding cheap tokens are used to offset debts in major assets.

What it doesn't prove: the reserve side. The project's verifier config describes the totals as information "published by CEX, it represents CEX's liability." The reserve figures are checked a different way, against the wallet addresses Binance publishes through the page's "Download All Address" option.

What customers can do: each user can get a Merkle proof for their account and check it against the published root. They can use the verifier code in Binance's repository rather than Binance's own interface. That doesn't prove Binance is solvent, but it confirms the user's balance was counted.

Binance has rebuilt its reserves to 100% across its ten largest assets, but on several of them the buffer is only a few coins. Meanwhile, stolen funds are reaching its deposit addresses through platforms that run on its infrastructure. Tuesday's proof can confirm customer balances. It can't show how Binance handles the stolen money arriving at its own door.
